memory_verse: "He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit." —Romans 8:11, NASB
sermon_title: A Freedom Only Christ Can Give

days.message_reflection: The sermon described an 'external life certificate' that looks good to others but carries a disclaimer that it says nothing about the inner life God actually sees. Thinking honestly about your own life this past week — not what others observed, but what you know was on the inside — what would the disclaimer on your certificate say?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:4 says the righteous requirement of the law is fulfilled in us who walk 'not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit' — and Romans 8:11 grounds this in the same Spirit who raised Christ now living in us. Are you relying on outward rule-keeping to produce inward change, or are you actually turning to the indwelling Spirit as the only real power to transform your thoughts, motives, and attitudes day by day?

days.focus: What God Sees That Others Cannot
days.message_reflection: The sermon pointed out that we can spend an entire life hearing good things from people around us and mistake that approval for God's approval — only to stand before the Lord and find that the one thing that mattered, the inside, was neglected. Is there any area of your inner life — a thought pattern, a motive, an attitude — that you have been content to leave unaddressed because no one else can see it?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:6 says 'the mind set on the flesh is death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace.' The Spirit who gives life to our mortal bodies (Romans 8:11) begins that work in the mind. When you sit quietly before God — not in a meeting, not in front of others — what does the direction of your habitual thinking reveal about what your mind is actually set on?

days.focus: Jesus Came to Set Captives Free
days.message_reflection: The sermon emphasized that Jesus chose this passage as his very first sermon — after 4,000 years of waiting — because his burning burden was for people who had a good external testimony in the synagogue but were in bondage to sin on the inside all week long. Do you honestly recognize yourself as one of the captives Jesus came to proclaim release to, or have you quietly concluded that your level of bondage is manageable enough to live with?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 6:14 declares 'sin shall not be master over you, for you are not under law but under grace' — and Romans 8:11 tells us the very Spirit of God dwells in us to make that a living reality. Zac Poonen often pressed this point: grace is not permission to sin, it is power not to sin. Is 'grace' functioning in your daily life as a genuine liberating power over a specific sin that has mastered you, or has it quietly become a comfortable explanation for why you keep failing?

days.focus: The Sick Who Know They Are Sick
days.message_reflection: The sermon drew a sharp contrast between those who maintain a clean external cup and those who are willing to 'tip the cup over' and let God see what is inside — and said Jesus came for the second kind, not the first. Are you currently approaching God and this church as someone who is well and managing, or as someone who is genuinely sick inside and desperate for the physician?
days.verse_reflection: Paul's anguished cry in Romans 7:24 — 'Who will set me free from the body of this death?' — is answered immediately in Romans 8:2: 'the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death,' and Romans 8:11 shows us that this same Spirit is not an external force but one who dwells in our mortal bodies. Have you actually cried out with Paul's desperation about a specific area of inner bondage, or has a degree of respectability before others kept you from the honesty that real freedom requires?

days.focus: Do You Wish to Be Well?
days.message_reflection: The sermon highlighted that Jesus did not ask the man at Bethesda whether he could make himself well — he asked whether he wished to be well. The sermon then applied this directly: some have tried for many years to be free from specific sins like anxiety, lust, anger, or bitterness, failed repeatedly, and have quietly settled for the condition. Honestly answer the question Jesus asked: do you genuinely wish to be well, or have you in any area made peace with your bondage?
days.verse_reflection: Galatians 5:16 says 'walk by the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desire of the flesh' — a present-tense, practical, daily promise that connects directly to the Spirit who gives life to our mortal bodies in Romans 8:11. The word 'walk' means step by step, moment by moment, not a one-time crisis experience. Is there a specific recurring desire of the flesh — in your thought life, your reactions, your secret habits — where you are not yet walking by the Spirit but are instead managing, suppressing, or rationalizing it?

days.focus: Grace and Humility as the Path to Freedom
days.message_reflection: The sermon brought together two realities: God is opposed to the proud but gives grace to the humble, and sin shall not be master over those who are under grace. The sermon pointed to humility — the posture of genuinely saying 'I am sick, I cannot fix this myself, Lord what do you think of my life?' — as the condition for receiving this grace. As you close out this week, in what specific area have you been too proud to fully admit the inside of the cup to God and ask for his cleansing, rather than just maintaining the outside?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:11 is the memory verse for this week: 'He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit.' Romans 8:9-10 just before it makes the condition plain: 'if the Spirit of God dwells in you.' The same power that overcame death is available to overcome sin in your body — your actual body, with its actual habits and cravings and emotional reactions. After this week of reflection, can you point to even one concrete moment where you turned to this indwelling Spirit for life rather than relying on your own willpower or the pressure of other people's opinions — and what would it look like to do that deliberately on Monday?
